name: Heldai
overview: Heldai was a male member of the tribe of Judah known as the Netophathite of Othniel. He held a significant leadership role as the overseer of the twelfth division during King David's reign, as noted in 1 Chronicles 27:15. His position indicates a trusted administrative responsibility within the organized tribal structure of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Heldai means 'mole' in Hebrew, a proper name recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:15. There is no indication that this name was given by God, but it identifies him distinctly within the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Heldai beyond his tribal affiliation with Judah and his role as the Netophathite of Othniel. No other familial connections are noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Heldai's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his leadership over the twelfth division of Israel during King David's administration. This role reflects the organized governance and military structure established under David, highlighting Heldai as a figure of authority and responsibility within the tribe of Judah. His mention in 1 Chronicles 27:15 underscores the detailed record-keeping of David's officials and their tribal origins.
